title: Helios-AI Architecture Spec v1 (Month 3)
author: Linh & Huy
content:
# Helios-AI Architecture Specification v1 (Month 3 - 2025-03)

Authors: Linh (AI Engineer), Huy (Backend Lead)

## 1. Vector Store & Embeddings (MVP)
- Vector Database: Qdrant collection `helios_mvp_768d`.
- Embedding model: `nomic-embed-text` (768 dimensions) running on single-node Ollama.
- Retrieval strategy: Dense vector similarity Top-K = 10, no cross-encoder reranking.

## 2. Large PDF Ingestion Policy v1 (Month 3)
- Mode: synchronous `POST /ingest` blocking HTTP connection until parsing completes.
- Concurrency policy: `max_concurrency = 8` parallel workers parsing PDF pages simultaneously.
- Memory policy: full chunk list buffered in memory; HTTP timeout = 120s.

## 3. LLM Routing (MVP)
- All requests route directly to a single model (`gpt-4o-mini`) with no router tier.

# Helios-AI Q1 Baseline Benchmark Report (Month 3 - 2025-03)

Author: Linh (AI Engineer)
Dataset: 120 real enterprise Q&A queries across 4 pilot teams.

## Baseline Metrics at Month 3

title: Postmortem #INC-064: Large PDF Ingestion OOMKilled (Month 6)
author: Dũng & Huy
content:
# Incident Postmortem #INC-064: Worker OOMKilled on Large PDFs (Month 6 - 2025-06)

Authors: Dũng (DevOps/QA), Huy (Backend Lead)

## Incident Summary
In Month 6, an enterprise customer uploaded 15 scanned technical PDFs (180-250 pages each) concurrently.
Under the Month 3 v1 policy (synchronous `POST /ingest` and `max_concurrency = 8`), worker pod memory spiked to 14.2 GB RAM and Kubernetes terminated the AI pod with OOMKilled (Exit Code 137).

## Permanent Remediation (Supersedes Month 3 Policy)
Effective Month 6, Helios-AI deprecated synchronous ingestion and `max_concurrency = 8`:
1. Switched `POST /knowledge/ingest` to async `202 Accepted` backed by a bounded `IngestionJobQueue` + `GET /knowledge/jobs/{job_id}` polling.
2. Reduced PDF ingestion `max_concurrency = 2` (hard-capped at 2 concurrent workers) to keep peak RAM below 2.5 GB.
3. Enforced streaming page extraction and `EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE = 32`.

title: Helios-AI Architecture Spec v2 (Month 6)
author: Linh & Huy
content:
# Helios-AI Architecture Specification v2 (Month 6 - 2025-06)

Authors: Linh (AI Engineer), Huy (Backend Lead)

## 1. Hybrid RRF Retrieval + Jina Embeddings v3
- Upgraded embedding model from 768d Ollama to Jina Embeddings v3 (`jina-embeddings-v3`, 1024 dimensions) in Qdrant collection `kb_jina_v3_1024`.
- Enabled Hybrid RRF (Dense + Sparse BM25) followed by Cross-Encoder Reranking.

## 2. 3-Tier LLM Routing
- Router tier classifies query intent quickly before specialist invocation.
- Specialist tier executes multi-step RAG and workspace workflows.
- Default synthesizer tier produces grounded user responses and handles fallbacks.

## 3. Large PDF Policy v2
- Confirmed post-#INC-064 policy: async `202 Accepted` ingestion queue with `max_concurrency = 2`.

title: ADR-019: Dedicated Autoscaling PDF Workers & Concurrency Update (Month 12)
author: Huy & Dũng
content:
# Architecture Decision Record ADR-019: PDF Worker Autoscaling (Month 12 - 2025-12)

Authors: Huy (Backend Lead), Dũng (DevOps & QA)
Status: Active (Supersedes Month 6 & Month 9 `max_concurrency = 2` cap)

## Decision
1. Dedicated 4 GB RAM autoscaling PDF worker pods with isolated memory cgroups are now deployed in production.
2. Under `IngestionJobQueue` (keeping async `202 Accepted` + `GET /knowledge/jobs/{job_id}` polling), the active PDF ingestion concurrency limit is raised from `max_concurrency = 2` to **`max_concurrency = 4`**.
3. Month 3's synchronous `POST /ingest` and `max_concurrency = 8` architecture remains permanently prohibited.

title: Helios-AI SOC2 Readiness & Multi-Tenant Security Standard (Month 12)
author: Huy & Dũng
content:
# Helios-AI SOC2 Type I Readiness & Multi-Tenant Compliance Standard (Month 12 - 2025-12)

Authors: Huy (Backend Lead), Dũng (DevOps/QA)

## Mandatory Guardrails
- Strict Multi-Tenant Isolation: Every Qdrant search/upsert and LangGraph checkpoint lookup validates `space_id`; zero cross-workspace leakage is enforced.
- Service Auth & Observability: `X-Internal-Key` + HS256 delegation JWTs protect internal APIs, Prometheus `/metrics` tracks token and error budgets, and runtime containers execute as non-root user `flux`.
